lines.text: King Agrippa and Bernice came down to Caesarea to pay their respects to Festus.
Festus said the chief priests and elders in Jerusalem requested a judgment against Paul, but he refused to hand him over before he could defend himself.
Paul's accusers charged him with none of the expected crimes, only disputes about their religion and a Jesus whom Paul said was dead.
When Paul appealed to the Emperor, Festus ordered him held until he could send him to Felix.
Festus found Paul had done nothing worthy of death and brought him before Agrippa to have something to write.
